author: Pennant, 1769
habitat: 민가 부근 숲, 산림, 사찰 주변 숲, 침엽수림
summary: 마을 가까운 숲과 산림, 절 둘레의 숲, 침엽수림에 사는 흔하지 않은 텃새이다. 오래된 큰 나무의 구멍에 둥지를 틀지만 건물 처마 밑을 쓰기도 하며, 5~6월에 알을 3~5개 낳는다. 밤에 활동하며 작은 포유류, 새, 파충류, 양서류, 곤충 따위를 잡아먹는다. 전국에 사는 것으로 짐작되며 국외에서는 동아시아에 분포한다.

points.en: grey-brown plumage with irregular black streaks

art.subject: Indian Scops Owl (Otus bakkamoena), adult of the Korean resident population: plumage grey-brown, finely vermiculated and marked with irregular black streaks; prominent ear tufts; pale greyish-buff facial disc with a thin dark rim; whitish eyebrows; a pale buff-grey collar across the hindneck, sometimes visible; a row of buff-white spots on the scapulars; underparts buff to greyish-buff with bold black shaft streaks and fine wavy cross-bars; legs and toes feathered. Iris orange-red to red, rarely yellow.
art.pose: perched upright beside a tree hollow at night, ear tufts raised
art.scene: Korean woodland of large old trees and conifers at night, an old trunk with a nest hollow; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, front view perched: raised ear tufts, orange-red eyes, pale facial disc with a dark rim, buff underparts with bold black shaft streaks and fine cross-bars, feathered toes
adult, side view perched: grey-brown upperparts with irregular black streaks, buff-white scapular spots, pale buff-grey collar on the hindneck
rare yellow-eyed individual, head close-up from the front: same face pattern and ear tufts but with yellow irises
art.build: Small, stocky owl, 24cm, clearly larger and heavier than the Oriental Scops Owl, about the length of a Brown-eared Bulbul but much bulkier; big rounded head with conspicuous ear tufts that can be raised or flattened. Bill short and hooked, mostly hidden in the facial feathers. Legs and toes feathered greyish-buff. Wings fairly short and rounded. Sits upright, pressed against a trunk with the ear tufts raised when alarmed.
avoid: Do not paint bare toes; legs and toes are feathered (Oriental Scops Owl has bare toes).
Do not make yellow eyes the normal colour; most birds have orange-red to red eyes.
Do not paint a long slim body with an orange facial disc — that is Long-eared Owl.
Do not paint it tiny and slim like the Oriental Scops Owl; it is bulky.
